title: Everyday Science II: Physics & Chemistry
desc: Units, light, electricity, elements, acids and materials

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the:
questions.e: F = ma; one newton accelerates one kilogram by one metre per second squared.

questions.q: The SI unit of energy is the:
questions.e: Work and energy both use joules.

questions.q: The SI unit of power is the:
questions.e: One watt is one joule per second.

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is the:
questions.e: One pascal is one newton per square metre.

questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the:
questions.e: One hertz is one cycle per second.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.e: It is measured with an ammeter.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric potential difference is the:
questions.e: It is measured with a voltmeter.

questions.q: The SI unit of resistance is the:
questions.e: Ohm's law states V = IR.

questions.q: The SI unit of sound loudness is generally given in:
questions.e: The decibel is a logarithmic unit.

questions.q: The SI unit of luminous intensity is the:
questions.e: Lumen is the unit of luminous flux; lux is illuminance.

questions.q: The SI unit of temperature is the:
questions.e: Absolute zero is 0 K, or -273.15 C.

questions.q: The speed of light in a vacuum is about:
questions.e: It is 299,792 km/s.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air is about:
questions.e: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.

questions.q: Sound waves are:
questions.e: They need a medium to travel.

questions.q: Light waves are:
questions.e: They can travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: The bending of light when passing from one medium to another is called:
questions.e: Dispersion is splitting of white light into colours, as in a prism.

questions.q: The splitting of white light into seven colours is called:
questions.e: VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red.

questions.q: The colour with the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum is:
questions.e: Violet has the shortest wavelength.

questions.q: The lens used to correct short-sightedness (myopia) is:
questions.e: A convex lens corrects long-sightedness (hypermetropia).

questions.q: A mirror used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles is:
questions.e: It gives a wider field of view.

questions.q: A mirror used by dentists and in shaving mirrors is:
questions.e: It forms magnified images at close distance.

questions.q: Newton's first law of motion is the law of:
questions.e: An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a force.

questions.q: Newton's third law states that:
o: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Objects tend to stay at rest
questions.e: Rockets work on this principle.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately:
questions.e: It is about 1/6 of this on the Moon.

questions.q: Weight is measured in:
questions.e: Mass is measured in kilograms.

questions.q: The device used to measure atmospheric pressure is a:
questions.e: A hygrometer measures humidity; an anemometer wind speed.

questions.q: The device used to measure earthquakes is a:
questions.e: The Richter scale measures magnitude.

questions.q: The device used to measure the humidity of air is a:
questions.e: A lactometer tests milk purity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.e: Silver is the best conductor, but copper is widely used.

questions.q: The fuse wire in a circuit is made of material with:
questions.e: It melts and breaks the circuit when overloaded.

questions.q: Domestic electricity supply in Pakistan is:
questions.e: The USA uses 120 V, 60 Hz.

questions.q: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.e: Oxygen is about 21 percent.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for sodium is:
questions.e: Potassium is K; iron is Fe; gold is Au.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for potassium is:
questions.e: From the Latin 'kalium'.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for iron is:
questions.e: From the Latin 'ferrum'.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for gold is:
questions.e: Ag is silver (argentum).

questions.q: The chemical name of common salt is:
questions.e: Its formula is NaCl.

questions.q: The chemical name of baking soda is:
questions.e: Washing soda is sodium carbonate.

questions.q: The main constituent of marble and limestone is:
questions.e: Chemical formula CaCO3.

questions.q: The pH of pure water is:
questions.e: Less than 7 is acidic; more than 7 is basic.

questions.q: Lemon juice is acidic because of:
questions.e: Vinegar contains acetic acid and sour milk lactic acid.

questions.q: The gas used in fire extinguishers is mostly:
questions.e: It displaces oxygen and cools the fire.

questions.q: The lightest gas is:
questions.e: Helium is the second lightest and is used in balloons.

questions.q: The gas responsible for the greenhouse effect most is generally considered:
questions.e: Methane and water vapour also contribute.

questions.q: The ozone layer protects the Earth from:
questions.e: It is located in the stratosphere.

questions.q: The metal that is liquid at room temperature is:
questions.e: Bromine is the only liquid non-metal.

questions.q: The alloy of copper and zinc is:
questions.e: Bronze is copper and tin; steel is iron and carbon.

questions.q: The rusting of iron needs:
questions.e: It is an oxidation process producing iron oxide.

questions.q: Which colour of light is scattered most and makes the sky blue?
questions.e: Shorter wavelengths scatter more (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.q: The unit of work is the:
questions.e: Work = force x distance.
